newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Schiffer seething over Colombian army ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Schiffer seething over Colombian army ad campaign.

text.p: Supermodel Claudia Schiffer is talking to her lawyers about an unauthorised ad campaign by the Colombian army featuring a photo of her wedged between two soliders, her publicist said on Tuesday.

"Claudia had absolutely no idea that these pictures were to be used for any kind of campaign. She's absolutely outraged. She is furious and deeply upset and has asked her lawyers to look into this," Fran Curtis, her New York-based publicist, said in a telephone interview.
The posters show the blonde German model sandwiched between a rifle-wielding infantryman and a parachutist above the slogan "National Army -- a Model of Virtues".
Curtis said Schiffer posed with the soldiers during a three-day photo shoot in Colombia in July, but thought they were only going to keep them as personal souvenirs.
An army spokesman said the posters had been distributed to battalions across the country as part of an internal image-boosting campaign, which cost just $5,000.
He said a Colombian magazine photographer supplied the photos of Schiffer but conceded that the army did not have publishing rights.

"The slogan to the posters tries to reflect the army's values of respect, duty and heroism. We had Schiffer wear a long skirt for the photos to give the image of a 'Model of Virtues' in all senses," another army spokesman said.
